libm.why: The one transcendental implementation the ops module calls: pure Rust, the same bits on arm64, x86_64 and wasm32.

serde.why: Derives the document model's serialization; it moves values and computes nothing from them. A facade over serde_core.

serde_core.why: The traits and impls serde re-exports; moves values, computes nothing from them.

serde_derive.why: The proc macro behind serde's derives: runs in the compiler and ships no code of its own; the code it generates calls serde_core.

proc-macro2.why: Token handling for serde_derive; runs in the compiler only.

quote.why: Token quoting for serde_derive; runs in the compiler only.

syn.why: Rust parsing for serde_derive; runs in the compiler only.

unicode-ident.why: Identifier tables for proc-macro2; runs in the compiler only.

serde_json.why: Parses and prints documents; its float formatting is shortest-round-trip (exact), and a check reads the parsed values, never the text's layout.

zmij.why: serde_json's float printer: the shortest text that reads back to the same f64, exact by construction; a check never reads the text.

itoa.why: serde_json's integer printer; a check never reads the text.

memchr.why: Byte search in serde_json's parser; integer code only.

indexmap.why: The insertion-ordered map behind serde_json's preserve_order: iteration follows insertion, never a hash; integer code only.

equivalent.why: Key-equivalence traits indexmap uses; no computation.

hashbrown.why: The table indexmap holds its indices in; indexmap never iterates it in hash order; integer code only.

foldhash.why: hashbrown's hasher as indexmap uses it, for lookups only; integer mixing, and no order a check reads comes from it.

allocator-api2.why: Allocator traits hashbrown is generic over; no computation.

sha2.why: Integer-only hashing for digests and hash@1 keys; the same bits everywhere by construction.

digest.why: The hashing traits sha2 implements; integer code only.

block-buffer.why: The input block buffer sha2 fills; integer code only.

crypto-common.why: Shared trait definitions for digest; no computation.

generic-array.why: Fixed-size arrays typed by length, for digest outputs; no computation.

typenum.why: Type-level integers for generic-array; resolved at compile time.

subtle.why: Constant-time equality for digest outputs; integer code only.

cpufeatures.why: Detects CPU features once so sha2 picks an accelerated path; every path gives the digest SHA-2 specifies, so the choice never reaches a check.

libc.why: The FFI bindings cpufeatures reads the feature flags through; nothing a check reads.

cfg-if.why: A compile-time cfg macro sha2 and cpufeatures use; no code of its own at run time.

unicode-normalization.why: Table-driven NFC for the canonical form of names; integer and string code only.

tinyvec.why: The small vector unicode-normalization buffers code points in; integer code only.
